title: Sacred Concerts and Duke's religion; the number written for Cootie
summary: Duke read the Bible many times; he wrote a Sacred Concert piece for Cootie after trying it out on piano.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: That was a nice suite. Then, in '65, well

that's when it really began, when he started the Sacred Concerts. And -- you know, I would just like to speak to you about that for a second. You know, he was working on that at Grace Cathedral, wasn't he, and the West Coast.
Uh-huh.
Well, Duke was a religious man.
Yeah.
And he always was a religious man, wasn't he?
Yeah, he was.
Yeah. So it was quite a logical thing for him to do the sacred music.
Yeah. Because he'd read the Bible through and through, many times.
Yeah. So it was something that everybody could feel for, doing the Sacred Concerts. I guess it was quite an exciting concept for everybody, wasn't it?
Yeah, it was. You know, the number that he wrote for me --
Which?
"The Shepherd".
Oh, yes. Of course.
It was a funny thing. First he was playing it on the piano. He wasn't playing it, he was just running it over. He called me down and said, "Hey, Coots, come

here." He said, "How do you like this number? Do you think you would like to play this number?" I said, "Yeah." I said, "I'll play it." So he wrote a lead sheet out on it. So I started messing around with it. He said, "What do you think of it?" I think it was about a week. I said, "Give me a chance. Give me time to feel the thing, so I can get something out of it." So we made an arrangement on it. So I started to playing it. He said, "Yeah, uh-huh. Yeah." "You're right." And that's how that number come about.
Isn't that terrific. That is wonderful. So, I mean, until you played, he didn't know what he -- he didn't have it, until you played it, really.
No.
Yeah. Then there was the number.
There was the number.
Yeah. That's wonderful. Who played that after you?
I don't think nobody.
Nobody.
No.
No. I guess he didn't play it again, did he? After he -- '73, or whatever, you know, when you stayed back, you know?
Yeah.
When it was a bad time. Well, --
Well, in '73, you know, I taken sick.
